highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.152.0 introduces Graphite GPU bindings and backend-neutral asynchronous pixel readback.
highlights_body: Built on Skia m152, this release adds Silk.NET Vulkan helpers and explicit font loading on Nano Server, while correcting source lifetimes and reducing text and data-copy overhead.

bullets.detail: Updates the renderer to milestone 152 and VulkanMemoryAllocator to 3.4.0, preserving the allocator fallback used by SkiaSharp callers.

Adds contexts, recorders, recordings and texture wrappers for Vulkan, Metal and Dawn, including browser WebGPU. Graphite uses explicit record, snap, insert and submit operations; existing Ganesh APIs remain unchanged.

Adds RequestReadPixels to SKImage and SKSurface. Results are callback-scoped: copy data inside the callback to retain it, and handle a null result on failure. Ganesh completion requires submission and CheckAsyncWorkCompletion; Graphite surfaces use asynchronous rather than synchronous readback.

Adds SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET with typed backend-context and extension helpers, and makes the GRVkExtensions constructor public. The existing SharpVk package remains available; package production now includes the Silk.NET helper.
Region iterators retain their source region, and pixmap subsets and With* results retain the ultimate pixel owner, preventing premature finalization while derived objects are still in use.

Releases the previous uniform buffer on Reset, disposes copied stream assets when HarfBuzz blobs release them, and frees raster pixel storage when image creation fails. Native cached-data destruction now releases its mutex guard before deleting the owner.

Font.Shape avoids copying an existing feature array, tag formatting avoids boxed characters, and text marshalling and uniform lookup construction allocate less. SKData.SaveTo writes native spans directly on span-capable targets; .NET Framework and netstandard2.0 retain buffered copying.

bullets.lead: Do not read stale GPU textures
bullets.detail: Ganesh readbacks no longer return stale texture data when prerequisite render tasks fail to flush; additional font-rendering and Ganesh stability corrections are included.

The Nano Server native build uses FreeType so fonts loaded from files, streams or data can render. It still has no system font manager: load a typeface explicitly rather than relying on the default font. Normal Windows builds retain DirectWrite.

Produces separate Apple symbol packages with complete dSYM bundles for SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp, without adding symbols to customer runtime packages. Android libraries retain matching build IDs and split-debug identities.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: Enabled FreeType-backed font loading on Windows Nano Server.
contributor_summaries.mmitche: Reduced Windows native build overhead by initializing the Visual C++ environment once per build.
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Introduced Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal and Dawn.

preview_summaries.v4.152.0-preview.1.1: Introduced Skia m152, Graphite, asynchronous pixel readback and Silk.NET Vulkan helpers. Also enabled explicit Nano Server font loading and corrected region, pixmap and failed-image source lifetimes.
preview_summaries.v4.152.0-rc.1.26426.14: Reduced shaping and tag-formatting overhead, corrected uniform-buffer and blob-stream cleanup, restored Silk.NET package production and added native debugging assets.

harfbuzz_summary: Font.Shape avoids a defensive feature-array copy, and Tag.ToString avoids character boxing. Apple symbol packages and deterministic Android debug identities improve native diagnostics; NuGet READMEs provide package-specific guidance.

v4.152.0-preview.1.1.headline: Preview 1 introduced Graphite, asynchronous pixel readback, Silk.NET Vulkan helpers, Nano Server font loading, and source-lifetime fixes.

v4.152.0-rc.1.26426.14.headline: The release candidate reduced shaping allocations, fixed uniform-buffer and blob-stream cleanup, restored Silk.NET package production, and added native debugging assets.

v4.152.0.headline: SkiaSharp 4.152.0 finalizes the release with a cached-data lifetime correction.
v4.152.0.body: The native mutex guard is released before its owning cached-data object is deleted.
